newsitem.title: JAPAN: Showa Denko may close naphtha cracker in May.
newsitem.headline: Showa Denko may close naphtha cracker in May.

text.p: Showa Denko KK said on Wednesday it may close one of the two naphtha crackers at its Oita plant on Japan's southern island of Kyushu for about two weeks in May due to technical problems.
"We haven't reached a final decision yet, but we may close it to replace a mechanical part that has not been working properly," a company spokesman said.
He declined to elaborate on the problem.
A two-week shutdown at the 220,000-tonne-per-year unit could mean lost ethylene production of about 9,000 to 10,000 tonnes, which would be produced from around 40,000 tonnes of naphtha, he said.
The other cracker at the plant has the capacity to produce 510,000 tonnes of ethylene a year.
The petrochemical firm last week announced that it planned to operate the two crackers at 90 percent of capacity until September because of high naphtha prices.
The firm may increase that rate if the unscheduled shutdown is carried out, he added.
